input.body:
label: bug
file: src/util/dates.ts

`isRollupDue` correctly computes the local hour for the recipient's time zone via `localHour`, but it also calls `startOfWeek(now, user.timezone)` to check whether `now` falls within the first day of the user's week. `startOfWeek` ignores the `tz` argument entirely (see the `// TODO: honour tz` comment) and always computes the Monday-00:00 boundary in UTC.

For a user in Sydney (UTC+10/+11), local Monday 08:00 is still Sunday (UTC) for much of the day, i.e. it falls *before* the UTC week boundary that `startOfWeek` computes. So `now.getTime() - weekStart.getTime() < DAY_MS` fails at the moment local time says Monday 08:00, and the rollup isn't sent until the next qualifying tick once the UTC-based week start has caught up — effectively pushing the email to Tuesday local time. Users close to UTC (e.g. London) don't see this because their local Monday 08:00 is close enough to the UTC boundary that the check still passes.

Fixing `startOfWeek` to actually compute the week boundary in the given time zone (rather than UTC) should resolve this for users in time zones far from UTC.
